answers.implementation_then_now: The answer is the lowest option on both dates: no national-law right to vote, because national electors are citizens only (Código Electoral Nacional art. 1). So implementation is Does Not Apply on both dates. For context, at the subnational level, which this indicator does not count, Chequeado reports that foreign residents voted in provincial and municipal elections both in 2023 (949,168 foreigners enrolled in Buenos Aires Province) and in 2025 (1,015,233 enrolled for the 7 September 2025 provincial election). Formosa remained the only province with no foreign-resident vote. Practice did not shift.

answers.sourcing_note: The InfoLEG consolidated Código Electoral shows art. 1 last replaced by Ley 26.774 (B.O. 02/11/2012). Its list of amending norms shows Ley 27.781 (Boleta Única Papel, Oct 2024) in the window, but that law did not touch art. 1. Constitution art. 37 has been unchanged since 1994. Ley 25.871 art. 11 carries no amendment note: DNU 366/2025 repealed other articles, such as art. 110, but not this one. Because nothing changed, the current text is the text that stood on both dates.

Ley 11.700 Provincia de Buenos Aires, Extranjeros – Régimen electoral
Constitución de la Provincia de Buenos Aires

answers.starting_answer_concern: The starting citation misreads Constitution art. 37. Its text (read) says only: 'Esta Constitución garantiza el pleno ejercicio de los derechos políticos... El sufragio es universal, igual, secreto y obligatorio.' It says nothing about provinces setting their own electoral regimes; that autonomy comes from arts. 5 and 121-123. The decisive national provision is Código Electoral Nacional art. 1: 'Son electores los argentinos nativos y por opción... y los argentinos naturalizados'. A reviewer could also argue for 'Right to vote in local or regional elections', since 23 of 24 jurisdictions grant it through provincial or CABA law. Those are subnational instruments, though, and the starting answer's choice to code national law only is kept.
answers.notes: No change in the window. Subnational law (e.g. PBA Ley 11.700 art. 1 and Constitution art. 191 inc. 2; the CABA Electoral Code art. 10) gives foreign residents the vote locally, and resident migrants actually vote in large numbers. This is context only, under a national-law coding.

provisions.instrument: Constitución de la Provincia de Buenos Aires (1994)

answers.implementation_then_now: The answer is the lowest option on both dates. National offices require citizenship (Constitution art. 48: 'cuatro años de ciudadanía en ejercicio'; art. 55: 'haber sido seis años ciudadano de la Nación'). So implementation is Does Not Apply on both dates. Buenos Aires Province's constitution, art. 191, lets registered foreigners with five years' residence stand as municipal councillors, capped at one third of a council. It was unchanged between 2023 and 2026. I found no practice evidence for the period on foreign candidates, and none of a shift.
answers.sourcing_note: The national constitution has not been amended since 1994, and the text was read on InfoLEG. The Buenos Aires Province constitution (normas.gba.gob.ar) shows art. 191, with the Ley 14.523 note: that law, of 2013, only declared a reform of inc. 3 (age 21) necessary. Nothing in the window. I did not open a provincial version-history portal, but provincial constitutions have no amendments in 2023-2025 on record.

sources_opened.title: Constitución de la Provincia de Buenos Aires

answers.starting_answer_concern: The starting citation names 'Art. 191.3' as the source of foreigners' eligibility as councillors. The text read says inc. 3: 'Serán elegibles todos los ciudadanos mayores de veinticinco años... y si son extranjeros, tengan además cinco años de residencia y estén inscriptos en el registro especial', and inc. 6 caps foreign councillors at one third. The attribution is broadly right. The claim that Buenos Aires Province is the 'only' such jurisdiction was not verified. As with q91, a local-office answer could be argued from subnational law, but the national-law coding is kept.
answers.notes: No change in the window. Confidence is medium because I found no practice source on foreign candidates. That gap does not affect the answer, since the national-law answer is the lowest option.
